title: Investigate and remediate int8 kernel-selection + KV-cache alignment causing silent accuracy drift and intermittent crash loops
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Summary: Following the rollout of the quant-autotuner-v2 release to production GPU pools, we observed two correlated failure modes for a subset of models on int8 execution paths: (1) silent accuracy degradation on long-context summarization and reranking workloads (quality regression without obvious error logs) and (2) intermittent crash loops on nodes running a fused-attention kernel when sequence lengths hit 2048+ under burst load. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigations, and action items to prevent recurrence.
impact: Approximately 12% of requests to the int8 model variants for a small set of customer workloads saw measurable ROUGE/accuracy drop; ~3% of serving replicas experienced crash-restart loops during bursts over three non-overlapping production windows (2025-01-09 to 2025-01-10). Affected customers were automatically failed over to float16 variants via emergency routing but saw increased latency and cost during the incident.
timeline: 2025-01-09 03:10 UTC: Alert - elevated error-rate from GPU pool cluster-gamma; initial signal attributed to OOMs on a small subset of pods.
2025-01-09 03:25 UTC: SRE routed traffic from int8 pool to float16 fallback policy; incident triage convened.
2025-01-09 04:00 UTC: ML quality team notified after customers reported decreased summary quality; initial hypothesis linked to autotuner changes.
2025-01-09 08:30 UTC: Engineering reproduced crash loop on test harness when executing fused-attention kernel at seq_len=2048 with int8 path enabled.

2025-01-10 12:00 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis refined: kernel selection + KV-cache pointer misalignment under certain batch/seq distributions causes stale attention masking and occasional invalid memory access.
2025-01-12 16:00 UTC: Hotfix PR merged to disable the experimental fused-attention kernel for int8 in prod; rollout completed to all clusters (runtime-1.20-hotfix-01).

2025-01-14 09:10 UTC: Quality regression investigation identified an edge-case in the autotuner that selected a lower-precision accumulation path when prefix-length distribution skewed long, producing silent metric drift.
2025-01-18 15:00 UTC: Action plan agreed with stakeholders and owners assigned. This ticket created to track remaining work and long-term fixes.
Links: see 'links' field for PRs, runbooks, and dashboards
root_cause: Two interacting defects: (A) Kernel-selection heuristic in quant-autotuner-v2 incorrectly preferred an experimental fused int8 attention kernel for certain batch/sequence distributions; that kernel contained an indexing edge-case that could produce invalid memory reads causing crash loops. (B) An accumulation-path selector allowed a reduced-precision accumulation (int8->int8 accumulation) for long-prefix workloads which, combined with a KV-cache pointer alignment bug under continuous batching, caused attention masks to effectively misalign leading to silent accuracy drift (lowered token probabilities for later tokens).
mitigation: Emergency mitigations applied: 1) Roll back / disable experimental fused-attention int8 kernel in production (runtime flag off). 2) Route affected customers to float16 variants automatically via existing fallback routing. 3) Throttle batch burst sizes on int8 pools as an interim to reduce KV-cache pointer churn. Hotfix PRs: runtime-1.20-hotfix-01.
action_items: Mateo Alvarez - Stabilize kernel selection: add deterministic guardrails in autotuner to prevent selection of experimental fused kernels unless validated by integration test matrix (estimate 5 pts, due 2025-01-24)
Aisha Khatri - Fix KV-cache alignment: audit and correct pointer arithmetic in KV cache codepath; add unit tests for continuous-batch edge cases and alignment checks (estimate 3 pts, due 2025-01-21)

Priya Rao - Recompute quality baseline: run regression evals across representative long-context prompts for top-10 affected models and publish delta report; attach to release notes (estimate 2 pts, due 2025-01-22)

SRE (Jackson Li) - Create and publish runbook for int8 crash loop detection and automated emergency rollback playbook; include dashboard alert thresholds for kernel OOMs and invalid-read patterns (estimate 2 pts, due 2025-01-20)

QA (Lena Müller) - Expand CI matrix: add seq_len stress tests (1024, 2048, 4096) with mixed batch sizes and KV-cache warm/cold scenarios for both int8 and int4 codepaths (estimate 4 pts, due 2025-02-01)
Product (Daniel Park) - Communicate with impacted customers: prepare customer-facing incident summary and mitigations, coordinate credits/compensations if required (estimate 1 pt, due 2025-01-19)
Infrastructure (Ruth Okoye) - Add capacity guardrails: limit burst concurrency per-host for int8 pools until autotuner safety gates are in place (estimate 1 pt, due 2025-01-21)

Research (Takahiro Sato) - Evaluate numeric stability: run controlled tests comparing accumulation strategies (int8->float32 accumulation vs int8->int16) and recommend default accumulation policy (estimate 3 pts, due 2025-01-30)

All - Post-deploy evaluation: once fixes are in prod, run a 72-hour canary on representative traffic with continuous metric comparisons and automated rollback on quality regressions (owner: Mateo Alvarez, due 2025-02-05)
postmortem_followup_notes: We will not mark 'Done' until: (a) autotuner guardrails are merged and rolled to prod, (b) KV-cache fixes pass the expanded CI stress suite, and (c) the 72-hour canary shows no quality regressions. Consider a small post-release retrospective with SRE, ML Quality, and Research to align on safety gates for future experimental kernels.
